subject: Post-call: sample pack & safety clarifications for model eval
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh@lexiflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: sample pack & safety clarifications for model eval

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Lexiflow's editor autopilot use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: reduce author editing time by surfacing targeted suggestions and automating boilerplate for legal templates (DOCX/HTML).
- Data shape: mixed short-form prompts (1-3 sentences), longer templates (200-1,200 tokens) and a small set of structured metadata fields (jurisdiction, document_type, sensitivity_flag).
- Latency SLO: median <= 220ms for short completions; batch jobs (bulk reprocessing) okay up to minutes.
- Privacy: some prompts include customer names and case numbers; Lexiflow would prefer that PII never leaves their VPC for production.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Model families to evaluate: Redwood-604B-quant (for long-template coherence) and Redwood-13B-q4f (for low-latency short suggestions). For a lightweight baseline, try Llama-2-13b-instruct-quantized. We'll include benchmark config in the Drive link below.
2) Eval plan: 3-stage approach — (a) small prompt set (250-500 samples) focusing on edge cases, (b) automated quality metrics (ROUGE, instruction-follow rate, prefix-safety checks), (c) human spot checks on 50 critical templates.

Action items I'm requesting from Lexiflow to kick off the eval:
- Share a sample pack (CSV or JSONL) with ~300 prompt examples across short-suggestion, full-template-complete, and redaction-sensitive cases. Mark any rows that contain PII with a sensitivity flag if possible.
- Provide one small schema sample (json) for the structured metadata fields.
- Confirm if you can share the sample data via a secured Drive link or if we should pull via an S3 bucket in your VPC.

I've attached a simple sample-capture CSV template (lexiflow_sample_prompts.csv) and a redaction checklist draft (redaction_guidelines_v1.docx) to help format the pack.

Marissa — can you take point on running the initial 300-sample eval once Lexiflow shares the pack? Ben — I'll need a rough quoted size for a 2-week dedicated eval sandbox (predictable capacity + 0.5 p99 uplift).

Suresh / Lexiflow team — can you send the sample pack by EOD Thu 4/19 (or let us know if you need more time)? If there are any constraints around PII transfer, flag them and we'll route to our Private deployment team (Mina) for a VPC/on-prem option.

Drive benchmark link: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/lexiflow-eval-v1
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/LF-2028-0042

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attach: lexiflow_sample_prompts.csv (CSV, template), redaction_guidelines_v1.docx (DOCX)
From: Suresh Patel <suresh@lexiflow.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lexiflow Data Team <data@lexiflow.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: sample pack & safety clarifications for model eval

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers / clarifications below: 

1) Sample pack: we can share a first pass CSV with ~320 rows by tomorrow EOD. We'll include a sensitivity_flag column where applicable. Some rows will contain names & case numbers that we'd prefer redacted for the hosted eval; we can provide a masked version and a VPC access option if needed.

2) Delivery: prefer to upload to an S3 bucket that you can pull from. We can grant a short-lived read role. Let us know the preferred bucket naming / IAM pattern.

3) Attachments: attaching a small schema (lexiflow_small_schema_sample.json) and a 10-row sample CSV (attached here as lexiflow_sample_prompts.csv). NOTE: the attached 10 rows are masked. The full pack will be delivered to S3.

4) Edge cases: we'll flag ~30 examples that trigger long legal clauses, nested placeholders, or multilingual fragments (EN/ES). We want to be sure the model doesn't hallucinate clause obligations. Any guardrails you recommend for hallucination risk?

5) Security: we have a SOC2 timeline — if we go the hosted eval route we need assurances that ephemeral copies are not retained beyond the eval window. If that's a blocker, we are open to Redwood Private (VPC) trial.

Next steps: we'll upload full pack to S3 (suresh-lexiflow-eval-20280419) and share credentials; confirm who on the Redwood side will accept the link.

Thanks — Suresh
Suresh Patel
VP Product | Lexiflow
Attach: lexiflow_small_schema_sample.json, lexiflow_sample_prompts.csv (10-row masked sample)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh@lexiflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: sample pack & safety clarifications for model eval

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround, Suresh. Short reply to lock down logistics and owners: 

- Delivery: Rafael (me) will accept the S3 link and coordinate the initial ingest. Please grant read-only, short-lived credentials to rafael_mendes@redwood.com. If any security team needs technical details for the role, loop Mina (cc'd).
- Hosted vs Private eval: if you can provide a masked pack first, we'll run the hosted sandbox to get initial signal on latency/quality. For any rows flagged as containing PII we will either (a) evaluate on masked inputs or (b) run those cases in a Private trial. Mina, please confirm the Private trial checklist and expected turnaround for a VPC test.
- Hallucination guardrails: our suggested checklist — 1) strict prefix matching for clause references, 2) allowlist of legal terms with fallback to "Escalate to human" for low-confidence generations, 3) temperature clamp (0.0-0.2) for template completions. We'll include these in the eval config. Marissa will run the bench with those settings and surface failure modes in a shared report.

Next steps & timeline: 
- Suresh: upload full pack to s3://suresh-lexiflow-eval-20280419 and DM the temp creds by EOD Fri 4/20.
- Marissa: kick off initial 300-sample run within 48 hours of access and post results to the Drive link.
- Mina: provide Private trial checklist / security sign-off ETA (target: 3 business days).
- Ben: produce a two-week eval quote for dedicated capacity and email to Suresh.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync next Tue to review initial findings; invite to follow. Thanks again — looking forward to the pack.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Attach: redaction_guidelines_v1.docx (DOCX)
